assignment:
Some of your friends perform community service. For example, some tutor elementary school children and others clean up litter. They think helping the community is very important. But other friends of yours think community service takes too much time away from what they need or want to do. 
Your principal is deciding whether to require all students to perform community service. 
Write a letter to your principal in which you take a position on whether students should be required to perform community service. Support your position with examples.
essay_1:
Dear Principal,

I am writing about whether students should have to do community service. I think we should, but only if the rule is fair and lets students pick what they do.

A lot of my friends already volunteer and I have seen how it changes them. My friend Maya helps second graders with reading every Thursday after school. At first she only did it cause her club needed hours. Now she talks about her kids all the time and she even makes up her own lessons. Another friend, Jake, picks up trash by the creek behind our school on weekends. He told me he never noticed how much garbage was there until he started picking it up. Now he wont even drop a wrapper on the ground. They probably would not have found this stuff if nobody made them try.

I know some people disagree. Lots of us have sports, jobs, or have to take care of family, and we already have a ton of homework. Community service could feel like one more thing to do. But I think this problem can be fixed if the school has a good plan. The school could ask for ten hours each semester, which is not that much when its spread out. Students should be able to count things they already do, like helping at a church food drive or watching their little brother or sister. That way the rule is fair for busy kids.

Also, community service teaches things you cant get from a textbook. You learn to show up on time, work with people who are different from you, and see that what you do matters to somebody else. Those skills will help us in college and at any job. The community gets something too, like cleaner parks and kids who read better.

For these reasons, I ask you to make community service a requirement with flexible hours and lots of choices. Some students might complain at first, but I think most of them will end up feeling proud of what they did.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
essay_2:
Dear Principal,

I am writing about community service. I think every student should do it, and I think it is a good plan when the rules are fair and kids get nice choices.

Some of my friends already volunteer, and it makes them happy. One friend tutors second graders in reading every Thursday. She loves it. At first she did it for club hours, and now she talks about her cute students and plans fun lessons on her own. Another friend joined a weekend group that cleans the creek behind our school. He says it feels great to see the creek look pretty, and he is proud to pick up each wrapper he sees. They found these good things because somebody gave them a push.

I know some kids think it is a bad idea. We have sports, jobs, and family chores, and homework takes a lot of time. Nobody wants a hard rule that feels like a problem. The school can ask for a small number of hours, maybe ten each semester, and let kids count the nice things they already do, like helping at a church food drive or watching a little cousin. A flexible plan is fair, easy for busy students, and friendly.

Community service also teaches good lessons that books can teach only a little. Students learn to be on time, to work with all kinds of people, and to be kind and helpful. Those are great habits for college and for any job. The town gets a lot of help too, like clean parks and happy kids who love to read.

So I hope you will pick a plan with fun choices and flexible hours. Some students may feel lazy at the start, and that is fine. Most of them will feel glad and proud, and they will be happy they tried. I would love to help make a good program for our school.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
